title: Builders in Villivakkam: Renovate or Rebuild Your Older House

seo.metaTitle: Builders in Villivakkam | Rebuild or Renovate | Hunter Property
seo.metaDescription: Older house in Villivakkam? We compare a full renovation with a rebuild for your plot, check the structure and the permissible area, then quote both options.

excerpt: Many Villivakkam houses from the 1980s and early 1990s are at the age where renovating and rebuilding cost about the same. This guide shows how to compare the two for your house and plot.
faqTitle: Rebuilding in Villivakkam: questions owners ask

faqs.question: What do your packages cost for a rebuild in Villivakkam?
faqs.answer: Our packages are priced per sq ft of built-up area: Basic ₹2,199, Standard ₹2,399, Premium ₹2,699 and Ultra Luxury ₹3,199. Approvals, soil test, compound wall, sump and interiors are quoted separately. For a rebuild we add demolition and debris disposal as separate lines, plus an access premium only if the lane blocks a transit mixer.

faqs.question: Who approves a rebuild in Villivakkam?
faqs.answer: For a typical individual house in Villivakkam, the building permit comes from the Greater Chennai Corporation; larger buildings go to CMDA. A rebuild needs fresh approval, while a renovation that keeps the existing structure avoids that timeline.

faqs.question: What do you check on the first visit to an older Villivakkam house?
faqs.answer: Whether the house is load-bearing or framed, what area current setback, coverage and floor space rules would permit on the plot, the lane width and how the street drains in heavy rain. Then we put the renovation and rebuild numbers side by side.

faqs.question: Why does a serious renovation of an old house cost more than expected?
faqs.answer: Because it usually means rewiring throughout, replacing the plumbing and working around a structure that limits what can be opened up. Once those are in scope, renovation stops being the obviously cheaper option.

faqs.question: Can I add a floor to my existing Villivakkam house?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but a load-bearing house on a foundation never sized for another floor needs its footings strengthened first. It is doable, not cheap, and a structural read on the first visit tells you which side of that line your house sits on.
